title: File card: name and size, readable by the bot
gate: Gate A oracle-file-sent 54/54 (the file card: card#3, 10 parts; scripts/lib/cards.mjs), oracle-file-waiting 47/47 (the file waiting in the composer)
evidence: The sent card looks as the oracle's 1.0.3 card (fixtures/states/oracle-file-sent, a version exception, docs/decisions/0008): components/Cards.tsx FileCard + styles/cards.css, in a row of its own above the message's bubble: 300 x 72 on rgb 37, radius 22, a page mark (a sheet with four lines), the name (its kind kept apart so a long name loses its middle) and the size. Waiting, a file sits inside the composer above the words as the oracle's does (components/Attachments.tsx: half the row, 56 tall, page mark, name, size, a Remove button; the box grows to 136, radius 18). The composer takes pictures, text files and PDFs, four in all, 3 MB each, by Attach files, a paste or a drop (Composer.tsx); each is stored for the conversation at the send (chat/api.ts uploadAttachment; Barkpark reads the type from the bytes), and the message names a picture by id and a file by {id, name} (sendMessage). A file Barkpark refuses (400), or a computer that cannot take files (422 host_cannot_receive_attachments), sends nothing: a plain line says why and the words and the file stay in the box. The sent message shows the file card at once, and after a reload from the stored row (Barkpark's attachments[] carries the name; chat/useConversation.ts). scripts/behaviour.mjs: 3 picture rules, 6 file rules (a zip refused, nothing stored; a text file waits by name and size; Enter stores it once and names it by id and name, the card shows; a 400 keeps the draft; a 422 keeps the draft and the same draft then goes (control); a reload shows the card from the row, once). Live pictures: npm run turn:live -- --picture (2026-11-13; parity/live/picture.json). Missing: the live file run, npm run turn:live -- --file (written, not run: the bot must reply with a made-up code held only in the attached file; it writes parity/live/file.json); the size wording (B, KB, MB) is ours, not read from the oracle (the fixture keeps only its length); opening a file from its card.
